public_rationale: Reporting is consistent with very large OpenAI net losses, but this compound claim goes further: it says both companies can become profitable only through financial engineering. The reviewed records do not establish that necessity. The unspecified accounting basis also prevents a decisive score on the monetary assertion. Large net losses, operating losses, and cash burn cannot be treated as interchangeable.
limitations: Calendar 2025 and separate company thresholds are evaluator interpretations.
The OpenAI evidence is secondary reporting on audited statements.
The financial-engineering assertion has no defined earnings measure or time limit.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic lose tens of billions of dollars a year and can only reach profitability through financial engineering.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic will grow to become the largest, most-profitable companies on Earth, even though they lose tens of billions of dollars a year, and can only “reach profitability” through financial engineering.

from_speaker: lose tens of billions of dollars a year
can only “reach profitability” through financial engineering
our_interpretation: The opening prediction about becoming the largest companies is presented sarcastically. It is not scored as Zitron's forecast.
The ordinary reading of the loss assertion is annual net losses of at least $20 billion for each company. A combined total is another possible reading.
For the annual-loss comparison, use calendar 2025, the latest completed calendar year before the post. Do not annualize a partial year's losses.

Financial engineering means accounting or financing changes that create reported profitability without profitable underlying operations. Showing such adjustments exist does not establish that they are the only possible route to profitability.
The supplied passage does not identify an accounting basis or attribute the loss figures to a particular financial report. The contract therefore records an unknown basis.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable annual net-loss figures meet the threshold for both companies, and financial records establish that the profitability being asserted depends on accounting or financing adjustments rather than underlying earnings.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable annual net-loss figures fall below the threshold under the specified reading, or either company achieves the relevant profitability through underlying earnings without the alleged engineering.

evidence.explanation: The report is consistent with the scale of OpenAI's annual net-loss assertion. It also describes a large nonrecurring accounting charge; that does not establish the claimed necessity of financial engineering for future profitability.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A specified accounting basis and comparable annual statements for both companies would settle the loss component. Reconciled earnings showing the alleged dependence on adjustments, or profitable underlying operations without them, would address the profitability component.
